prompt:
Two quantum states with energies E1 and E2 have a lifetime of 10^-9 sec and 10^-8 sec, respectively. We want to clearly distinguish these two energy levels. Which one of the following options could be their energy difference so that they can be clearly resolved?
A. 10^-9 eV
B. 10^-4 eV
C. 10^-8 eV
D. 10^-11 eV

rounds.rationale: The energy difference must exceed the natural linewidths from the lifetimes (~10^-7 eV), and only 10^-4 eV is sufficiently large.
The energy uncertainty from the shortest lifetime (~10^-9 s) is about 10^-7 eV, so only 10^-4 eV is large enough to clearly resolve the levels.

prompt:

If |\uparrow\rangle and |\downarrow\rangle are the eigenstates of \sigma{z} , then what is the expectation value up to one decimal place, of the operator 10\sigma{z}+5\sigma_{x} ? Here, symbols have their usual meanings
A. 1.65
B. -0.7
C. -1.4
D. 0.85

rounds.rationale: Recomputing the expectation value gives 10(-0.5)+5(√3/2)≈ -0.7, confirming option B.
Recalculation confirms the expectation value is -0.7, so option B remains correct.

prompt:
trans-cinnamaldehyde was treated with methylmagnesium bromide, forming product 1.

1 was treated with pyridinium chlorochromate, forming product 2.

3 was treated with (dimethyl(oxo)-l6-sulfaneylidene)methane in DMSO at elevated temperature, forming product 3.

how many carbon atoms are there in product 3?
A. 10
B. 12
C. 14
D. 11

rounds.rationale: I kept D because the sequence adds one carbon from the Grignard reagent and one carbon from the ylide, giving a total of 11 carbons.
Grignard addition adds one carbon to cinnamaldehyde (C9 to C10), PCC preserves carbon count, and the sulfur ylide adds one more carbon, giving product 3 11 carbons.
